COLUMN CROSS-CHECK: three level-1 records agree for all five items -- ES2973 DATA LIST positions 30/38/39/46/47; ES2973 VARIABLE LABELS (/P1 'Frecuencia de audiencia en televisión de noticias', /P2 'Frecuencia de audiencia en televisión de programas económicos, sociales o políticos', /P3 'Frecuencia de escucha de radio', /P4 'Frecuencia con la que se escucha la radio de programas económicos, sociales o políticos', /P5 'Frecuencia de lectura de periódicos'); and the printed questionnaire's column markers (30) P.1, (38) P.2, (39) P.3, (46) P.4, (47) P.5. The labels are content-distinct (TV news / TV political programmes / radio news / radio political programmes / newspapers), so no two items can be swapped without being self-evident. Data corroborate: r(p3,p4)=0.59 (the radio pair) and r(p1,p2)=0.33 (the TV pair) are each item's highest correlation. TEXT (text_source=study_materials): item_text = the printed P.1-P.5 question wording, read visually from 200-dpi renders of cues2973tipoA.pdf page 1 (P.1-P.3) and page 2 (P.4-P.5); the PDFs are image-only scans with no text layer, so spot-check character by character is advisable. Versions A and B print P.1-P.5 identically (compared side by side on both pages; FT2973 says the versions differ only in P.9, 12, 15, 21, 24, 26, 29). Dropped: the 'P.1.'..'P.5.' numbering and the interviewer direction '(MOSTRAR TARJETA A).'; line wraps joined; the italic 'tablet' in P.5 shipped as plain text. P.1's lead-in 'Para empezar' and P.4's 'Y,' are part of the printed stems and kept. All five asked of all respondents: P.1 'Nunca' routes to P.2, P.3 'Nunca' to P.4 and P.5 'Nunca' to P.6, which skip only the follow-up days-per-week grids (P.1a/P.3a/P.5a, other tables), not these items. One trivial section_id, instructions/section_prompt blank. The interviewer's questionnaire prints code 2 as '3-4 por semana' (no 'días'); the card and value labels were preferred as what the respondent saw. All five items use all five levels.
